29.content:
Consent form


Study title: Are Musicians Able to Ignore Distracting Sounds?

Purpose of the Study: The purpose of this research project is to identify whether distracting sounds are inconsequential to a musicians memory performance or detrimental.

Study Procedures: Participants will be asked to wear headphones, and to complete a short series of questions regarding sounds presented through the headphones. This component takes less than 5 minutes. Following the headphone check procedure, participants will complete a number of trials in which they are asked to recall a series of numbers in order, using the mouse to click on the numbers that they saw. Sometimes, they will hear sounds through the headphones, and sometimes they will not. At the end of the recall trials, they will be asked 12 questions regarding their subjective experience in the memory task. Then they will complete a a musical test followed by a music questionnarie about their daily interactions with music.

Risks: There is no known risk. This study is confidential and any documents will be labeled with participant numbers, which will not be connected with your identifying information in any documentation.

Benefits: Participants will receive either course credit or extra credit in their Psychology classes, depending upon which course that they are taking. The study is designed to provide critical information about the nature of testing, and whether or not the type of testing plays a role in the size and presence of auditory distraction effects on immediate memory. The findings will have implications for the theoretical understanding of immediate memory, and how to best design interventions for auditory distractions.

Investigator: The following investigator is available for questions about this study

Matthew Jimenez- mjime16@lsu.edu

Performance Site: The study will be completed fully online.

Number of participants: Up to 160 participants who meet the inclusion criteria described below.

Participant Inclusion: Undergraduate Psychology students at LSU that are native speakers of English, have normal or normal-to-corrected vision, and self-report no hearing loss. School of Music students who have had more than 5 or more years of training.

Exclusion Criteria: Individuals under the age of 18.

Privacy: Results of the study may be published, but no names or identifying information will be included in the publication. Data will be kept confidential unless release is legally compelled.

Financial information: There is no financial incentive to participate in this study.

Right to Refuse: Individuals may choose not to participate or to withdraw from the study at any time without penalty or loss of any benefit to which they might otherwise be entitled.

Signatures: The study has been discussed with me and all my questions have been answered. I may direct additional questions regarding study specifics to the investigators. For injury or illness, call your physician, or the Student Health Center if you are an LSU student. If I have questions about subjects' rights or other concerns, I can contact Dr. Alex Cohen, Institutional Review Board, (225) 578- 8692, irb@lsu.edu. I agree to participate in the study described above and acknowledge the researcher's obligation to provide me with a signed copy of this consent form if signed by me.






Please press start on the next page to begin the next task. Please give the program a few minutes to load.
